title: The Queen of Saba
art: The prophets appear only as steady lights; kings, armies, the queen and the people as dim figures of light; the jinn as smouldering shadows. The look of the land is imagined.
The queen (named Bilqis in the commentaries) appears as a soft dim light. The floor of glass is drawn as a gleaming floor like water (27:44).
imagePrompt: A great palace hall with a floor of glass so clear it gleams like still water, a soft light of a queen stepping onto it, a steady light standing at its far end beside a tall throne; then the queen's light bowing; ink-wash and parchment texture.

beats.say: Sulayman sent the queen a letter calling her to God. She came to see him, and found her own throne already brought to his palace before her.
Enter the palace, she was told. Its floor was of glass so clear she thought it was water.
Then she understood. My Lord, she said, I have wronged myself; I submit with Sulayman to God, Lord of the worlds.

pendingVerse.part: her words, from "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself"
